config.title: Display Values

intro.title: Display Values
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that demonstrates how different CSS display values affect the layout and behavior of HTML elements. You will learn the core concept of the CSS display property and its common values like block, inline, and inline-block. The main technology involved is CSS, using style rules to control element presentation. By the end, you will understand how to use display values to create basic web layouts and control element flow.
intro.usecase: Understanding display values is essential for creating responsive layouts across modern web applications. Developers use display: flex to build navigation menus and card grids in e-commerce sites, while display: grid organizes dashboard panels and data tables. Display: inline-block controls button groups and form elements, and display: none toggles mobile menus and modal dialogs. Mastering these values allows you to structure interfaces efficiently, from social media feeds to admin panels.

objectives: Apply different display values to HTML elements to control their layout behavior
Configure block-level elements to flow vertically in the document
Implement inline elements that flow horizontally within their container
Construct layouts using inline-block elements that combine block and inline characteristics
Manipulate element visibility using the none display value
Initialize flex containers to create flexible one-dimensional layouts
Render grid layouts by applying grid display values to parent containers

steps.title: Create the HTML structure for display examples
steps.instruction: Create a container div with three child div elements that will demonstrate different display values.
steps.hint: Start by writing a div element with a class, then add three div elements inside it. Each inner div should have a unique class name.
steps.seedCode: /* Create a container div with three child div elements */
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic HTML structure ready to be styled with different display values in the next steps.
successCriteria: A container div exists with three child div elements, each with a unique class name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three child div elements inside the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a container div element with three child div elements inside it.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the container
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the container div with padding, a border, and a background color.
steps.hint: Use the selector for the container div and add properties like padding, border, and background-color.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create a container div with three child div elements */

/* Add your container styling here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have visible padding, a border, and a background color to create a clear workspace.
successCriteria: Container has padding, border, and background-color properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include padding, border, and background-color for the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container styling is missing or incomplete. Add CSS rules with padding, border, and background-color properties.

steps.title: Style the child elements for visibility
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style all three child div elements with padding, margin, border, and background color.
steps.hint: Target the child div elements inside the container using a CSS selector. Add properties like padding, margin, border, and background-color.
steps.expectedOutcome: The three child div elements will become visible with padding, margin, borders, and background colors.
successCriteria: All three child div elements have padding, margin, border, and background-color properties applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure all child elements have padding, margin, border, and background color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child elements are not styled as required. Check that you've applied padding, margin, border, and background-color to all child divs.

steps.title: Apply display: block to the first element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to set the first child div to display: block. Use a class selector for the first child.
steps.hint: You can target the first child using the class name you assigned earlier or a specific selector like .child:nth-child(1).
steps.expectedOutcome: The first child element will take the full width of its container, stacking vertically above the other elements.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a rule that sets display: block on the first child element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've correctly targeted the first child element and set display: block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for display: block on the first element is missing or incorrect. Review how to target the first child and apply the display property.

steps.title: Apply display: inline to the second element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to set the second child div to display: inline.
steps.hint: Target the second child element using a selector like :nth-child(2) and apply display: inline;
steps.expectedOutcome: The second child element will flow inline with other content instead of taking the full width.
successCriteria: The second child element has display: inline; applied in the CSS.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've correctly targeted the second child element and set display: inline;.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second element doesn't have display: inline; applied. Check your CSS selector and property.

steps.title: Apply display: inline-block to the third element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to set the third child div to display: inline-block.
steps.hint: Target the third child element and use the display property with the value inline-block.
steps.expectedOutcome: The third child element will behave like an inline element but allow width, height, and margin properties like a block element.
successCriteria: The third child element has display: inline-block applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're targeting the third child element specifically and using the exact value 'inline-block'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're adding a CSS rule for the third element with display: inline-block.

steps.title: Add text content to demonstrate inline behavior
steps.instruction: Add text content before, between, and after the three styled div elements to observe how different display values affect text flow.
steps.hint: You can add plain text directly in the HTML structure, outside of the div elements, to see how block, inline, and inline-block elements interact with surrounding text.
steps.analogousExample:
Text before element

Styled element

Text after element
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML structure will include text content placed strategically around the three div elements to visually demonstrate how each display value (block, inline, inline-block) affects the flow of surrounding text.
successCriteria: Text content is added before the first div, between the first and second div, between the second and third div, and after the third div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some text, but make sure to place text before, between, and after all three div elements to fully demonstrate the flow differences.
steps.feedbackWrong: The text content wasn't added as specified. Try adding plain text in the HTML structure around the three div elements.

steps.title: Create and style elements with display: none
steps.instruction: Add a fourth div element with the class 'hidden-element' and apply display: none to it.
steps.hint: Create a new div element after the existing three divs and give it a class name. Then write a CSS rule that targets that class and sets display to none.
steps.expectedOutcome: A fourth div element is added to the HTML structure and styled with display: none, making it invisible in the layout.
successCriteria: The code includes a fourth div element with a class and a CSS rule that sets display: none for that class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've both added the fourth div element and created a CSS rule with display: none targeting it.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a fourth div element and apply display: none to it using CSS.

steps.title: Create and style elements with display: flex
steps.instruction: Add a new container div with display: flex and three child div elements inside it to demonstrate flexible box layout.
steps.hint: Create a div with a class like 'flex-container', set its display property to flex, then add three child divs inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new flex container with three child elements will be created, ready for styling to demonstrate flexbox behavior.
successCriteria: A div with display: flex is added, containing three child div elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some flex-related code, but make sure you have a container with display: flex and three child div elements inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex container structure isn't complete. You need to add a div with display: flex and three child div elements inside it.

steps.title: Compare all display values side by side
steps.instruction: Add descriptive comments above each display value example to clearly label them for comparison.
steps.hint: Add a CSS comment (/* comment */) above each display property you've set to identify which display value it demonstrates.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each display value example will be clearly labeled with comments, making it easy to compare their visual behaviors side by side.
successCriteria: Comments are added above each display property declaration to identify block, inline, inline-block, none, and flex examples.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some comments, but make sure each display value example (block, inline, inline-block, none, and flex) has a descriptive label.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding CSS comments (/* comment */) above each display property to label which display value it demonstrates.
